summary: Twombly's plausibility standard extended to every civil action. The E.D.N.Y. denies the Attorney General's and FBI Director's motion to dismiss on qualified immunity, and they take an interlocutory collateral-order appeal to the Second Circuit. Exercises FRAP's interlocutory door and the 60-day notice-of-appeal window for federal officers.

legs.context: Javaid Iqbal sues federal officials over his post-9/11 detention (Elmaghraby v. Ashcroft, E.D.N.Y.); the individual defendants' Rule 12 window is open.

steps.event: Ashcroft and Mueller move to dismiss: the complaint pleads no facts showing their own involvement, so qualified immunity applies
Judge Gleeson denies the motion in relevant part

legs.context: The denial of qualified immunity is an appealable collateral order (Mitchell v. Forsyth, 472 U.S. 511 (1985)); the case restarts in the court of appeals' view of the order.

steps.event: The order is not a final judgment
Denial of qualified immunity turning on an issue of law is a collateral order
Defendants notice appeals (No. 05-5768 and six consolidated appeals); federal officers sued individually get 60 days
No cross-appeal (route assumed; none in the sources read)
Appeal from a ruling on the papers: no transcript to order (route assumed)
No stay motion in the sources read (route assumed)
Argued before Newman, Cabranes and Sack, JJ. (argument date not found; route assumed)
Qualified immunity on the pleadings is reviewed de novo, taking the allegations as true
Iqbal v. Hasty: affirmed in part, reversed in part (procedural due process claims), remanded
Mandate clock resumes (mandate date not in the sources read)
Ashcroft and Mueller petition for certiorari (No. 07-1015)

gaps.event: Defendants appeal the denial of their motion to dismiss immediately, as a collateral order
gaps.why: links.json joins FRCP to the courts of appeals only at notice-of-appeal-filed, i.e. after a final judgment. No link carries an interlocutory order out of the district court into FRAP's interlocutory door (collateral order, 28 U.S.C. 1292(a)/(b)). Closing it needs a new FRCP node for an appealable interlocutory order plus a link, not a one-line fix.

gaps.event: Supreme Court reverses and remands (argued 2008-12-10, decided 2009-05-18, 5-4): Twombly's plausibility standard governs 'all civil actions'
gaps.why: No pack models Supreme Court merits review; cert-granted is terminal.

deadlines.trigger_event: the order denying the motion to dismiss
deadlines.arithmetic: FRAP 4(a)(1)(B): 60 days when a U.S. officer is a party. Sep 27 + 3 = Sep 30; + 31 = Oct 31 (34); + 26 = Nov 26 (60), a Saturday; FRAP 26(a)(1)(C) rolls to Monday Nov 28.
deadlines.historical: Notice-of-appeal dates were not found; the lead appeal is No. 05-5768, i.e. docketed in 2005.
Petition filed 2008-02-06, about seven weeks after the unextended date. An extension under Sup. Ct. R. 13.5 is the usual explanation, but none was found in the sources read.

quirks: The FRCP pack has one 'motion denied' edge into answer-filed; a denial 'in part' is not distinguished.
The Second Circuit's own wording was 'affirm in part, reverse in part'; the Supreme Court's opinion describes it as affirming. The walk follows the circuit's judgment.
The FRAP pack routes every panel-rehearing denial through an en banc poll; the docket only records 'rehearing denied'.
